bullets.title: GOOGL: DeepMind CEO Hassabis steps down, Jeff Dean exits; stock falls 5%
bullets.body: Alphabet shares dropped 4-5% (~$200B market cap loss) after Google announced Demis Hassabis is transitioning from DeepMind CEO to Chairman, with Koray Kavukcuoglu taking over most responsibilities. Jeff Dean, Google's Chief AI Scientist, also departed to start his own company. Separately, Google is in talks for a $1.5B+ deal with AI coding startup Mechanize.

bullets.title: ANET: Best earnings call in years; all major bear thesis risks mitigated
bullets.body: Arista Networks reported its seventh triple play in two years (third consecutive), with shares up 4.6%. One analyst described last night's earnings call as 'one of the best in years,' noting that concerns over customer concentration, top account loss, and white box displacement all appear mitigated. GlobalFoundries Q2 read-through confirms AI optical-networking demand accelerating faster than supply.

bullets.title: NVDA: $100M bearish options flow vs. 4.3% stock gain; AI optical supply chain moves
bullets.body: NVDA shares hit a 2-month high, up ~4.3%, but saw nearly $100M in bearish options flow intraday. Separately, NVDA has secured $2B investments in each of Coherent and Lumentum with multibillion-dollar purchase commitments and capacity rights, positioning it ahead of downstream participants in the AI optical supply chain. NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Ultra also outperformed frontier models on Palantir customer tasks within 24 hours of testing.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR/AAOI: FCC ban on Chinese optical transceivers seen as major supply chain catalyst
bullets.body: A proposed FCC ban on Chinese data-center optical transceivers is viewed as a material market redistribution event for U.S.-based suppliers LITE, COHR, and AAOI. One analyst designates Coherent as the preferred structural position, citing vertical integration, indium-phosphide capacity expansion, and direct earnings sensitivity. Chinese optical module stocks sold off on the restriction rumors while domestic names stand to gain.

bullets.title: UBER: Q2 beats with 22% gross bookings growth; CEO bullish on AV rollout
bullets.body: Uber Q2 2026 posted its fourth straight quarter above 20% gross bookings growth (+22% YoY), with CEO Khosrowshahi citing strong consumer demand. Management expects fully autonomous vehicles on the Uber platform in 15 U.S. cities by end of 2026, with 100 paid self-driving rides (no safety driver) seen as the key stock catalyst toward $100. Waymo relationship described as 'strong.' Pershing Square holds UBER as third-largest position, down 15% in 2024.

bullets.title: AAPL: BofA reiterates Buy, $380 PT on 28% surge in purchase commitments
bullets.body: Bank of America maintained its Buy rating and $380 price target on Apple, pointing to a 28% surge in purchase commitments to $57 billion as a signal of an iPhone production ramp and component stockpiling ahead of the next cycle.

bullets.title: AMD: Datacenter revenue +107% YoY but AI guidance disappoints
bullets.body: AMD beat on revenue with datacenter segment growing 107% year-over-year, but forward AI guidance failed to meet Wall Street expectations, extending the pattern of AI hardware companies beating on results while guiding cautiously. One analyst dismissed the 'CapEx surprise' narrative, calling the $800M capex a sound investment.

bullets.title: MSFT: Nadella cites Morgan Stanley ROIC data showing 31% IaaS / 46% TaaS returns; Burry exits position
bullets.body: Microsoft's Satya Nadella highlighted a Morgan Stanley ROIC report showing 31% returns for hyperscaler IaaS and 46% for Token-as-a-Service layer as evidence of strong cloud economics. Separately, Michael Burry reportedly dumped Microsoft bets while warning of a potential major market top.

bullets.title: MU: Market cap crosses back above $1 trillion
bullets.body: Micron's market capitalization recovered above $1 trillion. A sales desk note flagged MU as a key data point worth tracking for semiconductor read-throughs.

bullets.title: NET: Q2 growth momentum intact; security emerging as incremental driver
bullets.body: Preview note for Cloudflare Q2 2026 indicates growth likely accelerated from Q1 with base case for 2H26 stable to modestly accelerating; security is emerging as the core incremental growth driver.

bullets.title: PLTR: U.S. Army alone accounts for $1.9B of $5.1B in federal contracts since 2010
bullets.body: Palantir has billed $5.1B in total U.S. federal contract obligations since 2010, with the Army representing $1.9B (over one-third), underscoring the company's deep government revenue base. NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra also outperformed on Palantir customer tasks within 24 hours, a positive data point for Palantir's AI deployment.

bullets.title: DIS: $24B content investment by FY26; theme parks outperforming vs CMCSA
bullets.body: Disney plans to invest $24B in content by fiscal year 2026, with cruise bookings appearing strong and China theme park bookings lagging. CEO D'Amaro took a swipe at Universal/CMCSA, claiming Disney is performing 'significantly better' than competition in theme parks after CMCSA sounded alarm on sector trends. YouTube competition for Disney+ flagged as a headwind.

bullets.title: GLW: Solar segment revenue +90% YoY to $438M in Q2 2026; U.S. polysilicon tariffs may restructure supply chain
bullets.body: Corning's solar segment (including Hemlock Semiconductor) posted Q2 2026 revenues of $438M, up 90% from $231M a year ago, though the segment recorded a $7M net loss. A U.S. polysilicon price floor and Section 232 tariffs are described as a supply chain restructuring event rather than conventional tariffs, potentially benefiting Corning as the most direct U.S.-listed beneficiary.

bullets.title: AMZN: Zoox launches first paid robotaxi rides in Las Vegas; Graviton/Trainium chip value metrics called inflated
bullets.body: Amazon's Zoox subsidiary is launching its first paid robotaxi service in Las Vegas. A separate critique noted Amazon inflates its AI chip value estimates by including internal software running on Graviton and Trainium chips, making the metric misleading for assessing actual third-party chip competition.

bullets.title: INTC: EMIB/Foveros packaging positioned to gain as AI shifts to inference and NVDA CoWoS capacity maxes out
bullets.body: An analyst argues Intel's EMIB and Foveros packaging technologies are positioned to capture share from TSMC's CoWoS as the AI market shifts toward inference workloads and Nvidia keeps CoWoS running at maximum utilization, creating allocation pressure that Intel can address.

bullets.title: T/VZ: Bernstein sees Starlink mobile as tactical threat, not existential; telecom stocks slide
bullets.body: Bernstein characterized Starlink's mobile launch as a 'jab, not a knockout blow' for U.S. telecom carriers, but AT&T and Verizon shares declined on the competitive overhang from Starlink's entry into mobile services.

bullets.title: SNDK: Analyst reiterates $2,450 PT with 'load the truck' conviction
bullets.body: An analyst reiterated a $2,450 price target on SanDisk (SNDK), describing it as offering superior risk/reward to the upside over a multi-year horizon and stating they would be aggressively buying at current levels—unusual directional language rarely seen in institutional research.

bullets.title: AXTI: Shares up 15% on strong price action; signal of buyer/seller tension
bullets.body: AXT Inc. (AXTI) rose 15% intraday with price action described as signaling a tug of war between buyers and sellers; trader noted uncertainty as to whether the move would hold.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA release could face another delay, bearish signal
bullets.body: A Rockstar developer signaled GTA could face another delay, which a trader flagged as 'definitely not good' for Take-Two Interactive.

bullets.title: NYT: Stock down 14% intraday
bullets.body: New York Times shares fell 14% during the session; no specific catalyst mentioned beyond the price action flag.
